newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on seasonal slide, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on seasonal slide, technicals.

text.p: A seasonal decline coupled with weak technical signals pressed CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
"There was better than expected harvest over the weekend because there was no rain. Now we wait to see the harvest progress reports this afternoon," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

USDA late Monday was expected to release weekly crop data showing the U.S. corn harvest as of Sunday was 35 to 40 percent complete. Last week (week ended October 15) 20 percent of the crop had been combined.
That's up from 14 percent the previous week but below the 36 percent pace a year ago and down from 34 percent average.
Traders said the market's drop late Friday kept prices in a technical downturn with the four and 20-day moving averages for the December remaining in a bearish mode.

The market was underpinned by a strong number in USDA's weekly export inspections report. USDA said corn export inspectations for the week ended October 17 were at 26.841 million bushels, up from 19.550 million the previous week.
Corn futures closed one to 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 1-1/4 at $2.79.

Support under the market came from Friday's USDA seven state Cattle On Feed Report which showed the number on feed as of October 1 at 7.486 million. That tally was three percent below a year ago but the trade was expecting the numbers to be almost five percent less than last year.

Short term technical indicators also have been slowing the slide in corn with the relative strength index (RSI) for December closing at 20.322 points. Traders generally view an RSI of 20 or less as indicative of a very oversold market.
Concerns about a slowdown in corn harvesting also were mentioned as a supportive factor with forecasts for showers this week in key combining areas garnering attention.
"Harvesting of corn is going to be slowed, maybe even halted in some areas, during the next seven days," said Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Indeed, after the close USDA reported U.S. corn combining in the U.S. Midwest as of Sunday at only 30 percent complete, below trade expectations for 35 to 40 percent.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 51,000 contracts, down from 67,205 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Cargill Investor Services sold 700 December $2.70 puts at 2-1/2 cents and Rosenthal Collins sold 400 December $2.70 calls at 10-3/4 cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 32,563 Friday.
